name: skeleton-arrow-after-death
comment: WP-4.6 review fix. An arrow whose shooter has left loadedEntityList still passes the dead skeleton object as the attacker (EntityArrow.java:163). Night (set_time 18000), difficulty 1. Stone: the skeleton's platform y = 60 over x -10..-3, z -3..3; the player's 1-block pillar (3, 60, 0) and waiting block (3, 60, 30); a floor y = 52 over x 8..14, z 0..7 with a fence pen (id 85) at y = 53 around x 8..12, z 3..7. t=1: player (id 0) at (3.5, 61, 0.5), skeleton (id 1) at (-5.5, 61, 0.5), wolf (id 2) in the pen at (10.5, 53, 5.5). The skeleton shoots arrow 3 in tick 2. t=3: an attack op without attacker kills the skeleton (damage 100), the player moves to (3.5, 61, 30.5) and its pillar is removed, so the arrow flies on and falls past x = 4. t=4: the player tames the wolf with a bone (EntityWolf.interact; tamed at once with seed 123, health 20, sitting). The skeleton is removed in tick 23 (deathTime > 20, EntityLiving.java:154-158). t=24: the player moves into the arrow's path at (9.5, 53, 1.5); the arrow hits it in tick 28. With the dead skeleton as attacker: EntityPlayer.attackEntityFrom scales the damage for an EntityMob at difficulty 1 (4 / 3 + 1 = 2: health 20 -> 18, EntityPlayer.java:366-378), alertWolves(skeleton) stands the sitting tamed wolf up and gives it the dead skeleton as target, which its next AI update drops (EntityCreature.java:24-25); the knock-back pushes away from the skeleton's last position (EntityLiving.java:337-345). The wolf then follows its owner and jumps at the pen fence. A null attacker (the port before this fixture) gives 4 damage, no knock-back (only a Math.random() attackedAtYaw, EntityLiving.java:346-348) and a wolf that stays sitting. rng_state and entity_state of ids 0..3 every tick, player_state every 10 ticks.
